description: Minimal Common Lisp CLOS model across three files: two root classes written with the mandatory EMPTY superclass list `()`, a single-superclass subclass, a multi-superclass subclass, and the multi-line form whose superclass list sits on its own line with a slot list beneath it. Exercises class and function extraction and package->function CONTAINS, and — the reason the fixture exists (#6370) — the defclass superclass list, together with the neighbouring forms that must NOT produce an EXTENDS: defstruct, defgeneric, and a malformed defclass whose first parenthesised group is a SLOT list.

expected_entities.name: animal
expected_entities.note: Root class: `(defclass animal () (slots…))`. The empty superclass list is CLOS's way of writing a root, and it is also the negative control for a producer that skips an empty group and reads the next one.

expected_entities.name: named
expected_entities.note: Second root, so the empty-list case is graded in two places and a producer special-cased to one class still fails.

expected_entities.name: dog
expected_entities.note: `(defclass dog (animal) …)` — the single-superclass form, all on one line.

expected_entities.name: hybrid
expected_entities.note: `(defclass hybrid (animal named) ())` — two superclasses in one list.

expected_entities.name: poodle
expected_entities.note: The multi-line form: name, then the superclass list on its OWN line, then a slot list. This is the shape the whole design turns on.

expected_entities.name: segment
expected_entities.note: `(defstruct segment (start) (end))`. Its first parenthesised group is FLAT, so it is the input that a producer wired into the defstruct loop would mis-read — see the forbidden row for it.

expected_entities.name: lonely
expected_entities.note: Deliberately malformed CLOS with NO superclass list, so its first group is the slot list. The class entity must still be extracted; only the edge must be absent.

expected_entities.name: zoo
expected_entities.note: The `(in-package :zoo)` namespace, held so the fixture measures more than the one edge kind #6370 adds.

expected_relationships.note: #6370: the plain single-superclass form. Varies nothing; it is the baseline every other row is measured against.
#6370: FIRST name of a two-name superclass list. A producer that takes only the first name of the list passes this row and fails the next.
#6370: SECOND name of the same list, and — with the poodle row below — the only place the multi-name split is graded. Varies the POSITION IN THE LIST, holding the class and the layout constant.

#6370: the multi-line form — superclass list on its own line, slot list beneath. The only rows that fail when the anchor's whitespace skip cannot cross a newline are this one and the next. It is also the only row whose owner and target sit in the SAME file, so it grades that the edge is anchored on the CLASS rather than on the file, which from_file narrowing could not otherwise distinguish.
#6370: the multi-name split again, but on the MULTI-LINE form and with a cross-file target. Varies the layout while holding the list length constant against the hybrid rows.

Pre-existing lisp behaviour, held so the fixture measures more than the one edge kind #6370 adds — and so a regression that dropped ALL embedded relationships is distinguishable from one that dropped only EXTENDS.
The same pre-existing edge in the file that also carries the new EXTENDS rows, so 'that file was extracted at all' and 'that file's hierarchy was extracted' fail separately.

forbidden_relationships.note: #6370 OVER-FIRING, slot list read as superclasses. `(defclass lonely ((name :initarg :name)))` omits the superclass list, so the group at the anchor is a list OF LISTS. NOT FIRED, and the reason is worth knowing before copying this fixture — it was found by SCORING, not by reading, and the first draft of this note claimed the opposite. TWO independent guards cover this input and they mask each other: deleting the nesting guard in lispBalancedGroup still emits nothing, because lispSuperclassNameRE is anchored at both ends and rejects the token `(name`. Firing this row takes two edits at once, which is not a mutant. The nesting guard is therefore graded at the UNIT level instead, by TestLispHierarchy_NestedFormInsideTheGroupEmitsNothing, on the one input that separates the two guards: `(defclass weird (base (extra)) ())`. This row stays as an absence fence for a producer with neither guard.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, empty list skipped. `(defclass animal () (name legs))` — the slot list is FLAT (slots with no options), so a producer that treats `()` as 'no list here' and reads the NEXT group emits the slot names as parents. FIRES, verified: making superclassEdges retry at the next group when the anchored one is empty makes the gate report exactly 2 forbidden hits — this row and the named row below — while must-have recall stays at 7/7, which is the whole reason forbidden rows exist. The slot list is flat ON PURPOSE: with `((name :initarg :name))` the same mutant emits nothing, because lispSuperclassNameRE rejects `(name`, and the row would have been decorative. Distinct from the lonely row: this class HAS a superclass list and it is empty, that one has none at all.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, empty list skipped, SECOND class, also with a flat slot list. FIRES under the same retry mutant — it is the second of that mutant's 2 forbidden hits. Two rows rather than one because they fail together only if the defect is general; a producer special-cased to one class name would keep this one.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, wrong def-form. `(defstruct segment (start) (end))` has a FLAT first group, so it is the one defstruct in this fixture that a hierarchy producer wired into the defstruct loop would actually emit for. FIRES, verified: adding the superclassEdges call to the defstruct arm of extractLisp makes the gate report exactly 1 forbidden hit, this row, with must-have recall unchanged at 7/7. CL's real struct inheritance is the `:include` option, which this change deliberately does not implement — pinned separately as TestLispHierarchy_DefstructIncludeEmitsNothing_KnownDivergence.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, slot list read as superclasses when a superclass list IS present. NOT FIRED by any of the 16 mutants scored, stated plainly rather than implied: reaching poodle's slot list requires BOTH crossing its real superclass list AND accepting a nested group, two independent edits, and neither alone gets here. It is an absence fence for a producer that takes the LAST parenthesised group, or the first group containing sub-lists — shapes a YAML rule pack produces naturally and a positional anchor cannot.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, direction. dog extends animal, not the reverse. NOT FIRED by any of the 16 mutants scored, and it cannot be — the edge is EMBEDDED on the owning record, so its source is the record it sits on and no single edit can transpose it. It is an absence fence for a producer that names source and target by capture group, which is a rule-pack shape rather than an extractor one; that exact defect is live today in internal/engine/rules/kotlin/frameworks/kmp.yaml (#6805). It is the only fixture row that would survive a whole-file edge count, which is why it is here despite being unfireable from this side.

forbidden_entities.name: ghost
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: `;; (defclass ghost (phantom) ())` is COMMENTED OUT in pets.lisp. NOT REACHABLE by any mutant of the hierarchy code, stated plainly rather than implied: stripLispStringsAndComments blanks a `;` comment to spaces offset-for-offset BEFORE any pattern runs, so neither the entity nor the edge can appear no matter how the superclass anchor is loosened. That scrubber is pre-existing; this row is an absence fence for a future producer that reads raw source (a YAML rule pack would fire here — internal/engine/rules/graphql/frameworks/graphql_schema.yaml does exactly that for commented-out SDL).

forbidden_entities.name: phantom
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: the superclass named in that same commented-out line. Same grading status as the row above — an unreachable fence, not a mutant-killed row.

forbidden_entities.name: spectre
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: `(defclass spectre (phantom) ())` inside the STRING literal bound to *doc*. Unreachable for the same structural reason — the scrubber blanks string contents too — and kept for the same reason.
